figures.caption: Figure 1: DPPE prevents the late-stage performance degradation observed in PRoPE. (a) Conceptual comparison between existing projection matrix–based positional encoding (left) and our proposed DPPE (right). Existing methods apply a single coupled SE(3) transformation [R | t] uniformly to the queries (Q), keys (K), and values (V) before attention. In contrast, DPPE, our proposed method, decouples the rotation R and translation t, and injects them into Q, K, and V according to their distinct geometric roles. (b) Novel view synthesis on MVImgNet2: Results represent the mean over three seeds, and the shaded regions indicate the standard deviation. PRoPE’s PSNR stagnates and degrades after 240k iterations, whereas DPPE remains stable.

Figure 2: Qualitative comparison of DPPE and PRoPE on MVImgNet2. DPPE recovers more detailed textures compared to PRoPE, indicating an improved ability to disambiguate camera parameters. DPPEtAdd produces slightly finer details than DPPEdual, reflecting its more explicit decoupling of rotation and translation.

Figure 3: Evaluation under extrapolation settings. We evaluate extrapolation capability with respect to the number of viewpoints and the zoom-in factor on MVImgNet2. DPPE constantly outperforms PRoPE in both settings. All values represent the mean over 3 seeds, and the shaded regions indicate the standard deviation.
Figure 4: Evaluation results of novel view synthesis on the MVImgNet2 dataset at each step. While the performance of GTA [20] and PRoPE [3] degrades, DPPE consistently improves the performance.

Figure 5: Extended NVS performance (PSNR) across six datasets. Results represent the mean over three seeds, and the shaded regions indicate the standard deviation. The learning curves show that our decoupled variants (DPPE and UCPE’s) consistently achieve superior or competitive robustness and training stability compared to coupled baselines.
Figure 6: Results for multi-view depth estimation with RoPE, PRoPE, and DPPE. Plot showing the L1 loss values smoothed via an exponential moving average (EMA) with a decay factor of 0.95.
Figure 7: Futher scaled-up training with PRoPE and DPPE. DPPE shows stable training behavior throughout the entire schedule while PRoPE suffers from training instability.
Figure 8: Qualitative comparison of DPPE and PRoPE for novel view synthesis on RealEstate10K.
Figure 9: Qualitative comparison of DPPE and PRoPE for novel view synthesis on SpatialVidHQ.
